eli: hi team, eli here (first week). trying to build runtime from source on a cloud linux VM. build fails at the final link with undefined references to cublasLt and a couple of cudnn symbols. followed the quickstart and used the tarball install of CUDA 12.2.

eli: link snippet:
```
/usr/bin/ld: CMakeFiles/runtime.dir/src/kernels/cuda_kernels.o: undefined reference to `cublasLtCreate'
/usr/bin/ld: undefined reference to `cudnnCreate'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

eli: nvcc --version: 12.2, driver: 525.89, lib paths under /usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib exist. I suspect a packaging mismatch.

sophia: welcome! :wave: quick checklist: 1) run `ldd build/runtime | grep -E "cublas|cudnn"` inside the container/VM; 2) ensure `/usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib` is on LD_LIBRARY_PATH or baked into rpath (`-DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=`). If ldd shows "not found" that's the immediate problem.

rachel: also confirm you installed cuDNN separately — toolkit tarballs sometimes omit cudnn. We pin CI to CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.9; using 12.2 is fine but check version compatibility.

eli: ldd shows `libcublasLt.so => not found` and `libcudnn.so => not found`. I did not install cuDNN.

sophia: install cuDNN deb/tar into the toolkit targets dir. Prefer the deb that creates proper symlinks: `dpkg -i libcudnn8_8.9.*_amd64.deb` (or unpack tar to `/usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib` and run ldconfig). Avoid manual symlinks unless for debugging.

rachel: additional tip — if objects were compiled with different C++ ABI or without PIC you can get weird link errors. If you see relocation errors, rebuild third_party with `-fPIC` or set `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON`.

eli: after installing cuDNN and running `sudo ldconfig` `ldd` now shows libs resolved but runtime crashes with `ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_86' is not supported by this toolchain` when some kernels compile.

sophia: that means your nvcc/toolchain doesn't recognize the arch flag. Check `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` in cmake cache; set it to the GPU's compute capability or use `Auto` to generate ptx fallback. Also ensure nvcc version matches the toolkit you installed (12.2 should support sm_86 but toolchain flags vary).

rachel: for onboarding, we recommend using the internal docker dev image `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-cudnn8-gcc11` to avoid these host mismatches. If you're on Mac hardware, request a cloud dev VM with GPU from infra.

eli: i'm on linux VM already but will try switching to the internal image. one more practical question: is it okay to set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` in my .bashrc to point to cuda lib paths during development?

sophia: it's fine for local dev but prefer baking rpath during cmake for reproducibility: `cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/targets/x86_64-linux/lib ..`. Also add a short note to your onboarding doc with the exact steps you followed so future new hires can avoid the same pitfalls.

oncall-bot: oncall-bot: If you need a pre-provisioned onboarding VM with matching stack, request `gpu-dev-onboard` in #eng-infra and include your username and desired CUDA (default: 12.1).

devops-bot: devops-bot: CI images are pinned to CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.9 + gcc-11. Using the internal `redwood/dev` image is the fastest way to match CI.

eli: thanks all, switching to the internal image now and will update this thread after a clean build. appreciate the help! :thumbsup:
